facts.statement: Ibirania is a genus of dwarf saltasaurine titanosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Southeast Brazil.
facts.quote: Ibirania (meaning "Ibirá wanderer" or "tree wanderer") is a genus of dwarf saltasaurine titanosaur dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Santonian to Campanian) São José do Rio Preto Formation (Bauru Basin) of Southeast Brazil.

facts.statement: Ibirania is one of the smallest known sauropods, comparable in size to Magyarosaurus.
facts.quote: It is one of the smallest sauropods known to date, comparable in size to the titanosaur Magyarosaurus.

facts.statement: Ibirania is estimated to have been only 5.7 meters long.
facts.quote: Ibirania is estimated to be only 5.7 m long, making it one of the smallest sauropods.

facts.statement: CT scans revealed that Ibirania possessed highly pneumatized vertebrae with a bird-like air sac system, a trait inherited from giant relatives despite its small size.
facts.quote: Using computed tomography, Aureliano et al. (2021) discovered highly pneumatized vertebrae in the Ibirania holotype.

facts.statement: Fossilized parasites were found preserved inside the vascular canals of an Ibirania bone lesion, representing the first such report in a dinosaur.
facts.quote: Aureliano et al. (2021) also discovered fossilized parasites associated with the bone lesions in Ibirania (LPP-PV-0043).

facts.statement: A partial fibula of Ibirania shows evidence of acute osteomyelitis, an infection that caused periosteal remodeling.
facts.quote: One of the specimens of Ibirania (LPP-PV-0043, a partial fibula) presented a pathology called acute osteomyelitis.

facts.statement: Ibirania coexisted with the abelisaurid theropod Thanos simonattoi, a large unnamed probable megaraptoran, and an indeterminate notosuchian.
facts.quote: It coexisted alongside other dinosaurs, such as the abelisaurid theropod Thanos simonattoi and a larger, unnamed probable megaraptoran, as well as an indeterminate notosuchian.

facts.statement: Ibirania is classified as a derived member of the Saltasaurinae, a clade containing some of the smallest titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Ibirania was a derived member of the Saltasaurinae, a clade known for encompassing some of the smallest titanosaurs.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Ibirania as the sister taxon to the clade formed by the Patagonian saltasaurines Bonatitan and Rocasaurus.
facts.quote: Ibirania was recovered as sister taxa of the clade formed by the Patagonian saltasaurines Bonatitan and Rocasaurus.

facts.statement: Additional referred material includes partial cervical, dorsal, and caudal vertebrae, fibula fragments, and a nearly complete fibula.
facts.quote: Additional material, including partial cervical, dorsal, and caudal vertebrae, fragments of a fibula, and a nearly complete fibula, was also referred to Ibirania.

facts.statement: Ibirania lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately between 86 and 75 million years ago (Santonian to Campanian stages).
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 86 a 75 millones de años, desde el Santoniense al Campaniense

facts.statement: The name Ibirania means "tree wanderer," combining the discovery location Ibirá with the Greek word for wanderer, reflecting its hypothesized browsing behavior.
facts.quote: The generic name, "Ibirania", combines a reference to Ibirá, the municipality where the specimens were discovered (also a Portuguese derivative of the Tupi word "ybyrá", meaning "tree", in reference to Ibiranias hypothesized browsing behavior), with "ania", a modified form of the Greek word "plania", meaning "wanderer".
